intro.text: The Foundry roars. Furnaces turn human-readable blueprints into machine code, and the blueprints keep coming back wrong.
Quack. The compiler is picky. Learn the order it works in and you will know where to look when it complains.

mid.text: The pipeline runs. But a furnace that melts the wrong metal is still broken: the bugs are in the blueprints.
Quack. Reading code line by line, out loud, to me, is half of debugging. Try it.

outro.text: Clean builds, clean output. A few small slips cost the Foundry a whole night. Now you know where they hide.
Quack. Next: Cipher Quarter, where text becomes arrays and secrets.

games.title: Spot the Slip
games.instructions: Each snippet has one bad line. Read the symptom, then click the line.

rounds.why: Every C statement ends in a semicolon.
string and get_string live in cs50.h, which was never included.

rounds.symptom: The program prints garbage instead of the age.
rounds.why: %s is for strings, but age is an int.
1 / 3 is integer division, which truncates to 0 before it's stored in the float.

rounds.symptom: Should print "meow" 3 times but prints it 4 times.
rounds.why: i runs 0, 1, 2, 3, which is four loops.
